history.period: Medieval (Thekkumkoor capital era, 15th-18th century); exact founding date UNVERIFIED
history.summary: Ancient Shiva temple near Uppoottikkavala at Thazhathangadi, Kottayam (CSV town corrected from Kottayam). Folklore: the Shiva idol was installed by Parasurama. History: after Venimala, Manikandapuram and Changanassery, Talikotta on the Meenachil River became the capital of the Thekkumkoor Kingdom, and the temple with the royal house was protected by the Thaliyilkotta fort, which gave the locality its name. From the early 15th century it was the royal temple of the Thekkumkoor dynasty - the Ariyittu Vazhcha (coronation) of about twelve kings took place before the Thali, and the 1419 land-transfer agreement that created the Poonjar state was signed in the temple's presence. After the 1750 Changanassery War the kingdom was annexed by Marthanda Varma's Travancore; the fort fell in 1749 but the temple was spared, then renovated by Dharma Raja (Karthika Tirunal Rama Varma), who gave pooja rights to Thuyyathu Bhattathiris from North Malabar. One of the 'eighteen-and-a-half thalis' of Kerala and one of four 'thali' temples in the 108-Shiva sothram (with Tali Kozhikode, Kaduthuruthy and Keezhtali Kodungallur) - distinguish it from the Kaduthuruthy Thaliyil Shiva Temple. Five daily poojas, Thazhamon Madom tantri; now under the Travancore Devaswom Board. The temple is noted for its murals and Kerala-style architecture.

name: Thaliyil (Talikotta) Mahadeva Temple
town_description: Thazhathangadi is a historic locality of Kottayam on the Meenachil River in central Kerala. It is known for the Thazhathangady Juma Masjid, one of India's oldest mosques, and for remnants of the Thekkumkoor royal era including the Thaliyil temple. Today it is a quiet, largely residential heritage pocket less than 2 km from Kottayam town centre.

travel.road: Less than 2 km from Kottayam town by road, at Thazhathangadi; reachable via local roads within Kottayam city
